---
title: "Get started"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

For your first Shiny form with unsaved-change tracking. This tutorial adds
a badge, saving, discard and a guarded record load.

## Track a form

List the input ids that belong to your form. Add `unsaved_badge()` to show
changes. The first values become the saved baseline. A changed field
gets a dot by its label.

This example stores a name in memory for this session only. Replace
`save_record()` with your app's storage code.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(unsaved)

ui <- fluidPage(
  unsaved_badge(),
  tabsetPanel(
    id = "tabs",
    tabPanel("Profile", textInput("name", "Name", "Ada"),
             actionButton("save", "Save"),
             actionButton("discard", "Discard")),
    tabPanel("Other", "Another page")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Replace this in-memory store with your app's save code.
  saved_name <- reactiveVal("Ada")
  save_record <- function() {
    saved_name(input$name)
    TRUE
  }
  tracker <- unsaved_track("name", on_save = save_record)
  observeEvent(input$save, tracker$save())
  observeEvent(input$discard, tracker$discard())
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Edit Name, then click Other. The guard asks before changing tabs.
Keep editing cancels. Discard and continue restores the saved value.
Save and continue runs `on_save` before continuing. The Save button uses
`tracker$save()` to run the same callback without changing tabs.
See [Saving](saving.html) for callback results, errors and background saves.

The default guards cover tab navigation and browser close or refresh.
Tagged buttons and links can also be guarded. See
[Modules and navigation](modules-navigation.html) for their scope and
[Limits](limits.html) for browser warnings.

## Inspect and discard changes

`is_dirty()` reports whether tracked values differ from the baseline.
`count()` gives the number of changed fields. `changed()` gives their ids.
These queries are reactive. `baseline()` returns the saved named list and
is not reactive. See [Server values and tables](server-values.html) for
`diff()` and field labels.

`discard()` requests restoration through the browser's input bindings.
It does not wait for restored values to return to the server.
If you supply `on_discard`, read `tracker$baseline()` there, not `input`.
Callback errors become warnings. See [Limits](limits.html) for supported
bindings and [Server values and tables](server-values.html) for server restoration.

## Confirm an action

`confirm(action)` runs a function with no arguments at once when clean.
When dirty, it asks first, even while paused. Keep editing cancels.
Discard restores inputs, calls `on_discard`, then runs the action once.
Save and continue runs it only after a successful save with no edits left.
Only one confirmation can wait per tracker. Further requests warn and are
dropped, not queued. Errors in the action warn without ending the session.

Use `confirm(action, text = unsaved_text(title = "Load another record?"))`
to set text for that dialog only. Capture the chosen record id before
asking if the action must use the selection made at that time.

## Loading a record

Set the saved baseline before sending input updates. This separate server
recipe assumes a tracker for `name` and `location`, two text inputs, a
record selector and a Load button. `records()` is your app's record store:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
observeEvent(input$load, {
  record_id <- input$record
  tracker$confirm(function() {
    record <- records()[[record_id]]
    tracker$load_baseline(values = record)
    updateTextInput(session, "name", value = record$name)
    updateTextInput(session, "location", value = record$location)
  })
})
```

`values` is a named list keyed by tracked input id. Omitted ids use their
current input values. Unknown ids are errors; password ids are ignored.
`load_baseline(values)` requires a named list. To acknowledge a completed save,
use `mark_saved(values = snapshot)`; it publishes the real state and keeps later
edits dirty. With no argument, `mark_saved()` captures current input values.

`load_baseline()` sends a clean state to the browser immediately.
Until the updated values return, server comparisons can briefly report
the old inputs as dirty.
The next server comparison decides the state; matching echoes leave it clean.
Supply values with the types returned by each input binding. Use `confirm()`
before replacing edits, as above.

The pause, update, wait for every echo, `mark_saved()`, resume pattern is still
useful when the final values are not known in advance, or updates span several
round trips. Disable editing and saving while that load is pending. Paused
queries still report real differences; `is_paused()` can show a loading state.
